claims.text: Oxidation resistance and material integrity in high-temperature MPEAs are governed by formation of a coherent, slow-growing protective oxide scale.
Sluggish cation diffusion in high-entropy systems enables selective enrichment and limited migration of Cr or Al.
Selective enrichment and limited migration of Cr or Al promote formation of stable protective oxides.
Alloys with lower concentrations of protective elements form less-uniform, faster-growing oxides.
Less-uniform, faster-growing oxides spall under thermal stress.
Incrementally increasing Cr or Al content is expected to enhance formation of a continuous, adherent protective oxide layer.
The controlled comparison will expose baseline and modified alloys to static-air oxidation at approximately 1100°C for 50 hours.
Oxide-scale thickness uniformity, phase composition, integrity, and adherence mediate oxidation behavior.
Reduced diffusion rates inherent in MPEAs control protective-scale integrity and adherence.
High mixing entropy in MPEAs reduces both cation and anion diffusion rates at high temperatures.
Reduced ionic mobility favors selective oxidation of enriched high-field-strength elements.
Limited ionic mobility produces a slow-growing, continuous, adherent Cr2O3 or Al2O3 scale.
A continuous, adherent Cr2O3 or Al2O3 scale mitigates further oxidation and spallation.
Insufficient protective-element content or faster diffusion causes nonuniform oxide growth and compromised integrity.
The Cr- or Al-enriched alloy will develop a thinner, more uniform, and more adherent oxide scale than the baseline.
The Cr- or Al-enriched alloy will show lower total oxidation weight gain than the baseline.
The improved oxide scale will correlate with better material integrity over the 50-hour exposure.
The baseline will exhibit faster oxidation, more scale spallation, and poorer structural integrity.
The proposed behavior is expected to hold at approximately 1000–1200°C in static oxidizing environments.
Equivalent oxidation behavior, or no statistically significant improvement in scale uniformity, weight gain, and adherence after increasing Cr or Al, would falsify the hypothesis.
